# Fexu — AI-readable documentation index

> Fexu is an experimental Rust web framework. As of 2026-11-20,
> the latest published Cargo workspace release is 0.1.2.
> The 0.2.0 target is planned and not yet published.
> The main branch may contain unreleased APIs.
> Always identify the documentation version and target source revision.

## Start here

- [Documentation home](index.md): source status, feature ownership, limitations
- [Quickstart](quickstart.md): current published CLI and source checkout paths
- [Models](models.md): macros, fields and repositories
- [Database](database.md): SQLite and PostgreSQL contracts
- [Migrations](migrations.md): read-only plans, apply, destructive safeguards
- [Authentication](auth.md): accounts, sessions and security constraints
- [Admin](admin.md): native admin behavior and limitations
- [Forms](forms.md): model/standalone forms and validation
- [CLI reference](cli.md): commands, flags and diagnostics
- [Configuration](configuration.md): env and project settings
- [Deployment](deployment.md): server, reverse proxy and runtime
- [Security](security.md): cookies, CSRF, dependencies and limits
- [Roadmap](roadmap.md): published vs development vs planned
- [Release candidate gates](release-candidate-0.2.md): the pre-0.2.0 release contract

## Important limits for AI assistants

- Do not infer that a feature in `main` exists in the published `0.1.2` crates.
- Do not recommend `cargo install fexu-cli --version 0.2.0` until 0.2.0 is actually available.
- Do not claim feature parity with Django, production readiness, OIDC support, working S3 networking, or cross-backend guarantees beyond those explicitly documented and tested.
- Do not guess Rust API signatures. When code matters, verify the release tag's real source and tests.
- Never advise applying destructive migrations or schema baselines without explicit approval and verified backups.
- Site snapshots under numbered versions describe their own release. `main` docs describe unreleased development.

This index aids discovery; it is not a substitute for source-backed validation.
